section_title: What kind of freedom and change does the Spirit bring?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 17 Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. 18 And we, who with unveiled faces all reflect the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

context_lines: Paul describes the removal of the veil in terms of the Lord’s Spirit and freedom. The setting is the Spirit’s life-giving work and release from the ministry of condemnation, not a claim that people are now free to disregard the Lord.

He then includes all the believers in the picture of unveiled faces. In the BSB they reflect the Lord’s glory and are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory. The change comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

This is God’s ongoing work in people, rather than a description of self-improvement achieved without Him. The language also reaches beyond one unusually gifted worker: Paul says all of them share in it.
The promise concerns a life increasingly shaped by the Lord. It should not be reduced to a demand that a faithful person must feel fearless or emotionally settled in every circumstance.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly understand these verses as freedom and transformation given through the Spirit in relation to Christ. [Wesley’s notes on verses 17–18](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-second-epistle-to-the-corinthians/) connect freedom with release from sin and growing likeness in love. The [USCCB notes on verses 17–18](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/2corinthians/3) connect it with release from condemnation and a change already begun in the community. Their focus is God’s work in His people, rather than permission to live without regard for Him.
god_plan_lines: [Romans 8:29–30](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/8.htm) describes God’s purpose for His people in terms of being conformed to the image of His Son. [1 Corinthians 15:49](https://biblehub.com/bsb/1_corinthians/15.htm) also looks ahead to bearing the likeness of the heavenly man in the discussion of resurrection.

These passages place present transformation alongside the future Christ promises. God’s purpose includes people becoming like His Son, with the Spirit already working in them as they await the completion of that hope.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
